status-ssh.text: Show the status of the SSH server with `systemctl status`. Think about what the service is called on Ubuntu!
status-ssh.hint: On Ubuntu the service is called `ssh`: `systemctl status ssh`.

failed.text: A service doesn't seem to have started. List all services that have *failed*.

journal-err.text: Show only the error messages (priority *err* and more severe) from the current boot in the journal.
journal-err.hint: `-p err` picks the priority and `-b` the latest boot: `journalctl -p err -b`.

journal-u.text: Read the log of the broken service `reportd` with `journalctl`. Why doesn't it start?
journal-u.hint: `-u` shows only the lines from one service: `journalctl -u reportd`. With `-xe` you jump to the end and get explanations.

fix.text: Fix the problem the log tells you about, then restart `reportd` with `systemctl` so that it runs.
fix.hint: The configuration file is missing, but there's an example: `sudo cp /etc/reportd.conf.example /etc/reportd.conf`. Then restart with `sudo systemctl restart reportd`.

start-myserver.text: Start the service `myserver` (unless it's already running) and then show its status. Which PID did it get?
start-myserver.hint: `sudo systemctl start myserver` and then `systemctl status myserver`.

stop.text: Stop `myserver` with `systemctl`. Feel free to check with `pgrep myserver` that the process is gone.

enable.text: Make sure `myserver` starts automatically every time the computer boots – and start it now as well, with a single command.
enable.hint: `enable` applies at boot and `--now` starts it right away: `sudo systemctl enable --now myserver`.
